questions.prompt: What is a group of buffaloes or elephants called? (A flock, B horde, C gang, D hedge, E herd)
steps: Herd is the collective noun for these large grazing animals.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: E. A herd.

questions.prompt: What is a synonym of purchase? (A sell, B buy, C selling, D exchange, E export)
steps: Purchase means buy.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: B. Buy.

questions.prompt: Hardly had I started closing my eyes ___ the bell rang. (A than, B but, C when, D where, E and)
steps: The construction is hardly...when.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C. When.

questions.prompt: Make passive: Ngulukenge is playing football at the playing ground.
steps: Move the object to subject position and use is being played to preserve present continuous.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: B. Football is being played by Ngulukenge at the playing ground.

questions.prompt: Make active: The chair was broken by Ken.
steps: Ken becomes the subject; was broken becomes past active broke.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: B. Ken broke the chair.

questions.prompt: Every day I wake up ___ and prepare for school. Bank: happy, early, big, begin, teacher, end, sad, small, pupil, slow, late.
steps: Early is the intended preparation time before school; late is possible only with a different routine.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Early.

questions.prompt: I feel ___ because I enjoy learning.
steps: Enjoyment supports happy.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Happy.

questions.prompt: I try to be ___ in class and finish work on time.
steps: Early fits punctuality. Slow contradicts timely completion, and the bank does not contain the natural adjective attentive.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Early is the most suitable available word, meaning arrive on time; there is no exact diligent/attentive option.

questions.prompt: We ___ lessons at 7:30 AM.
steps: Begin means start.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Begin.

questions.prompt: The library is ___; there is little space.
steps: The lack of space indicates small size.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Small.

questions.prompt: Match learn a lesson with A caning, B obey directions, C feel sorry, D classmate, E trembling, F written information, G feel guilty, H learn to prevent recurrence.
steps: The idiom refers to gaining understanding from an experience.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: H. Learn something so it does not happen again.

questions.prompt: Match cane.
steps: Cane is the verb described by the matching option.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: A. Beating someone with a stick for wrongdoing (definition in source).

questions.prompt: Match ashamed.
steps: Ashamed concerns embarrassment or guilt about an action.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: G. Feel guilty (best supplied option); C. feel sorry is related.

questions.prompt: Match statement.
steps: This is the source's intended description of a statement.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: F. Something written that gives information.

questions.prompt: Match obey.
steps: Obey means follow an instruction.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: B. Do what you are told.

questions.prompt: The bird flew ___ the tree and landed. (onto, towards, into, across)
steps: Onto emphasises arrival on a surface; the exact landing place is not shown.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Onto (intended landing on a branch); into is possible for entering the canopy.

questions.prompt: The cat jumped ___ the box. (into, onto, through)
steps: Without a picture, jumping inside, onto the top, or through an opening are all possible.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Into, onto or through, depending on the movement.

questions.prompt: The cow walked slowly ___ the farm. (across, through, from, onto)
steps: No destination or picture distinguishes the routes.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Across is likely intended; through/from/onto have other grammatical directions.

questions.prompt: Children went ___ the forest for firewood. (into, onto, across, through)
steps: Into describes entering the forest to collect wood.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Into is intended; through or across could describe a route.

questions.prompt: The dog ran ___ the gate after hearing noise. (into, onto, through, towards)
steps: Towards means approaching; through means passing the opening.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Towards or through; no unique direction is specified.

questions.prompt: Who is the health teacher at Maweni?
steps: The opening names her.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Ms. Jemima.

questions.prompt: What were the two pupils doing?
steps: The passage describes their behaviour.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Sharing one mango by biting from it.

questions.prompt: Who taught the pupils health habits?
steps: She addressed the assembly.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Ms. Jemima, the health teacher.

questions.prompt: Why should we avoid touching wounds without protection?
steps: Wounds can expose people to blood; this does not mean HIV spreads through ordinary contact or shared food.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: To reduce exposure to blood and germs that may cause infection.

questions.prompt: Order A-E: The guide allowed photographs and we enjoyed learning about nature.
steps: This follows the guide's explanation.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: D.

questions.prompt: Order: After an exciting day we returned home tired and happy.
steps: The return ends the trip.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: E.

questions.prompt: Order: Last weekend our school organised a national-park trip.
steps: Introduce the trip first.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: A.

questions.prompt: Order: On arrival we saw elephants, lions, zebras and cobras.
steps: Arrival follows the introduction.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: B.

questions.prompt: Order: The tour guide showed us the animals and explained their habits.
steps: The guide's explanation precedes photographs.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C.
